decision.question: Are the scene's surfaces and tonal values represented pervasively in a pencil-drawn shading style?
decision.criteria: Pass if tonal modeling across the principal objects and large surrounding surfaces is pervasively conveyed by pencil-like shading, including directional strokes, hatching, graphite-like rubbed tones or mark-based texture following form. Fail if substantial surfaces retain photographic tonal modeling, realistic specular reflections or photographic material textures merely covered by grain. Reduced saturation, softened contrast and a uniform texture overlay alone do not satisfy this condition. Retained patterns are not themselves disqualifying; evaluate whether their rendering and surrounding tones are pencil-drawn rather than photographic. Use unknown only when the available visual evidence cannot establish the shading style.
decision.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Inspect tonal rendering across the food, glassware and pitcher, as well as the large tabletop, tablecloth and surrounding background areas. Distinguish form-following pencil marks or graphite-like tonal rendering from retained photographic gradients, reflections, woven textures and printed patterns under an overlay.
